coverage: Complete play in both English editions: named cast, individual and collective speaker roles, the unnamed princess, mythic references and identifiable attendants. No invented names for the sons or princess.

entities.name: Medea
entities.body: The woman from Colchis, wife of Jason and mother of their two sons.

entities.name: Jason
entities.body: The Greek hero of the Argo’s quest, husband of Medea and father of their sons.

entities.name: Creon
entities.body: King of Corinth and father of Jason’s new bride.

entities.name: Creon’s daughter
entities.body: The princess of Corinth, Jason’s new bride. She is not named in this text.

entities.name: The nurse
entities.body: Medea’s elderly servant and confidante.

entities.name: The children’s attendant
entities.body: The elderly servant who looks after Medea and Jason’s sons.

entities.name: Medea and Jason’s sons
entities.body: The two young sons of Medea and Jason. Their personal names are not given.

entities.name: The first child
entities.body: One of Medea and Jason’s two sons, distinguished by his speaker label.

entities.name: The other child
entities.body: The other of Medea and Jason’s two sons, distinguished by his speaker label.

entities.name: The women of Corinth
entities.body: The local women who speak and sing as the chorus.

entities.name: The chorus leader
entities.body: The spokeswoman for the women of Corinth.

entities.name: A woman of the chorus
entities.body: An individual woman speaking from the chorus.

entities.name: Another woman of the chorus
entities.body: A second woman speaking from the chorus.

entities.name: Aegeus
entities.body: King of Athens and an old friend of Medea.

entities.name: The messenger
entities.body: A servant from the royal household who brings news to Medea.

entities.name: Pelias
entities.body: The king of Iolcus who sent Jason in search of the Golden Fleece.

entities.name: The daughters of Pelias
entities.body: The daughters of King Pelias, also called the Peliads.

entities.name: Pittheus
entities.body: The king of Troezen, son of Pelops, whom Aegeus plans to consult.

entities.name: Pelops
entities.body: Pittheus’s father, a king of Greek legend.

entities.name: Pandion
entities.body: Aegeus’s father in the Athenian royal line.

entities.name: Erechtheus
entities.body: A legendary king and ancestor associated with Athens.

entities.name: Zeus
entities.body: The chief god of the Greek pantheon.

entities.name: Themis
entities.body: The goddess associated with divine order, justice and sacred obligations.

entities.name: Hecate
entities.body: The goddess of magic whom Medea invokes as her special protector.

entities.name: Aphrodite
entities.body: The goddess of love, here called the Cyprian.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The legendary Greek singer and musician.

entities.name: Apollo
entities.body: The god whose oracle Aegeus consults at Delphi, also called Phoebus.

entities.name: Maia
entities.body: The mother of Hermes in Greek mythology.

entities.name: Hermes
entities.body: The divine messenger and protector of travelers, son of Maia.

entities.name: The Muses
entities.body: The nine goddesses of poetry, music and the arts.

entities.name: Ino
entities.body: A woman of Greek legend whom the chorus recalls as a mother driven mad by Hera.

entities.name: Hera
entities.body: The queen of the gods and goddess of marriage.

entities.name: Skylla
entities.body: The sea monster of Greek legend, also called Scylla.

entities.name: Athena
entities.body: The goddess of wisdom and protector of Athens, here called Pallas.

entities.name: Pan
entities.body: The rustic god whose influence was associated with sudden terror and frenzy.

entities.name: Helios
entities.body: The sun god, Medea’s divine grandfather.

entities.name: The old handmaid
entities.body: The elderly woman among the princess’s attendants in the messenger’s account.
